about: The learning agenda on /evidence-map/: questions the evidence on this site has not yet answered, one or more for each cycle whose evidence is still emerging. 'have' restates the limits the cited studies give themselves (see EVIDENCE in data/core); 'could' and 'scale' are our suggestions, shown as such. The monthly update may add questions, or mark one 'answered' with the record ids that answer it, under the same tone and evidence checks. Questions are never deleted.

questions.q: How much of the load on clinics in South and Southeast Asia during a heatwave is heat illness, and which early actions lower it?
questions.have: A global health assessment that does not give Asia’s share, and one before-and-after evaluation in Ahmedabad where other changes may explain part of the effect.
questions.could: Compare clinic records across hot seasons in cities with and without early-warning plans.
questions.scale: Two or three cities, two seasons

questions.q: How many heat deaths go uncounted, and which ways of counting close the gap?
questions.have: Official counts that rise partly because reporting improves, and part-season counts that show the gap but not the true toll.
questions.could: Compare excess deaths with recorded heat deaths in a few districts, and test simple reporting changes.
questions.scale: A few districts, one or two seasons

questions.q: Does money spent on prevention before summer reduce what is spent during heatwaves?
questions.have: One modelled estimate for Bangkok, multi-hazard estimates, and a review of heat plans as they stood in 2023.
questions.could: Track what a city spends before and during heatwaves over several seasons, with its health and work outcomes.
questions.scale: One or two cities, three seasons

questions.q: How often does heat illness lead households to borrow, and how much?
questions.have: Studies of household debt that do not measure heat’s part, and an older national survey of all medicine costs.
questions.could: Follow households through a hot season with a short monthly survey of illness, costs and loans.

questions.q: How do small firms and their lenders in Asia respond when a heatwave empties streets and shops?
questions.have: Evidence from rich economies and from Mexico, an industry statement naming heat among several causes, and one self-reported survey of vendors in Delhi.
questions.could: With willing lenders, compare microfinance repayments against daily heat records.
questions.scale: Two or three lenders, two seasons

questions.q: Who cannot afford to keep cool, measured directly rather than estimated?
questions.have: A global model that estimates the risk of lacking cooling from income, power and heat data.
questions.could: Add a few cooling questions to an existing national household survey.

questions.q: How much learning do children lose in hot classrooms and heat closures in Asia?
questions.have: Strong evidence from schools in the United States, and counts of closures in Asia that measure days lost rather than learning lost.
questions.could: Compare learning results with classroom temperatures over a school year.

questions.q: When heat cuts a harvest, how often does debt follow, and what helps farmers recover?
questions.have: A debated national association, and studies from single sites or single crops.
questions.could: Follow farm households across seasons, linking heat to yields, loans and recovery.

questions.q: When Asian cities add parks and trees, do rents rise and do residents move?
questions.have: A multi-city study with no Asian cities, mostly US reviews, and one qualitative study in Bangkok.
questions.could: Track rents and who lives where around new green spaces, before and after.

questions.q: Which street trees in humid Asian cities survive repeated heatwaves, and what care keeps them alive?
questions.have: Tree-loss figures from Berlin, and a global comparison of species’ natural climate ranges.
questions.could: Survey street-tree survival after each hot season, with watering and care records.

questions.q: Does heat, on its own, push people to move within Asian countries, and where do they land?
questions.have: Worst-case scenarios to 2050 that cover every climate driver together, not heat alone.
questions.could: Link existing migration surveys with local heat records.

questions.q: How large are uninsured losses from heat, and could money arranged in advance narrow the gap?
questions.have: Figures for all natural catastrophes together, and a qualitative regional review.
questions.could: Estimate uninsured heat losses for one sector in one country, and test a pre-arranged payout design.
